# Connect-ZbxServer

## SYNOPSIS

Connects the session to a Zabbix server with an endpoint and a credential.

## SYNTAX

### Anonymous (Default)

```
Connect-ZbxServer [-Uri] <Uri> [-Name <string>] [-Trapper <DnsEndPoint[]>] [-FrontendUri <Uri>] [-SkipCertificateCheck] [-AllowUnencryptedCredential] [-TimeoutSec <int>] [-Proxy <Uri>] [-ProxyCredential <PSCredential>] [-NoDefault] [-PassThru] [-TrapperTls <ZabbixTlsMode>] [-TrapperPskIdentity <string>] [-TrapperPsk <SecureString>] [-TrapperCertificate <string>] [-TrapperCertificateKey <string>] [-TrapperCertificateAuthority <string>] [-TrapperCertificateRevocationList <string>] [-TrapperServerIssuer <string>] [-TrapperServerSubject <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### ApiToken

```
Connect-ZbxServer [-Uri] <Uri> -ApiToken <SecureString> [-Name <string>] [-Trapper <DnsEndPoint[]>] [-FrontendUri <Uri>] [-SkipCertificateCheck] [-AllowUnencryptedCredential] [-TimeoutSec <int>] [-Proxy <Uri>] [-ProxyCredential <PSCredential>] [-NoDefault] [-PassThru] [-TrapperTls <ZabbixTlsMode>] [-TrapperPskIdentity <string>] [-TrapperPsk <SecureString>] [-TrapperCertificate <string>] [-TrapperCertificateKey <string>] [-TrapperCertificateAuthority <string>] [-TrapperCertificateRevocationList <string>] [-TrapperServerIssuer <string>] [-TrapperServerSubject <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Credential

```
Connect-ZbxServer [-Uri] <Uri> -Credential <PSCredential> [-Name <string>] [-Trapper <DnsEndPoint[]>] [-FrontendUri <Uri>] [-SkipCertificateCheck] [-AllowUnencryptedCredential] [-TimeoutSec <int>] [-Proxy <Uri>] [-ProxyCredential <PSCredential>] [-NoDefault] [-PassThru] [-TrapperTls <ZabbixTlsMode>] [-TrapperPskIdentity <string>] [-TrapperPsk <SecureString>] [-TrapperCertificate <string>] [-TrapperCertificateKey <string>] [-TrapperCertificateAuthority <string>] [-TrapperCertificateRevocationList <string>] [-TrapperServerIssuer <string>] [-TrapperServerSubject <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

Creates the client, asks the server apiinfo.version, proves the credential with one authenticated read (a -Credential logs in for it), and adds the connection to the runspace's context under -Name (the endpoint's host and port by default), as the current server unless -NoDefault; a token or a password the server refuses ends the command with an AuthenticationError that names the server (ZabbixApi.SessionTerminated or ZabbixApi.NotAuthorized for an unknown or disabled token, ZabbixApi.TokenExpired, ZabbixApi.LoginFailed) and adds nothing. A connection already under that name is closed once its in-flight calls finish. Secrets enter only as a PSCredential or a SecureString, never as a positional string. The TLS parameters (-TrapperTls, -TrapperPskIdentity, -TrapperPsk, -TrapperCertificate, …) are the trapper's: every command that speaks the server's own protocol (Send-ZbxData, Get-ZbxQueue, Get-ZbxServerStatus, Test-ZbxItem, Test-ZbxExpression, Test-ZbxMediaType) uses them unless it is given its own. They are checked here (the certificate files are read), and the API's HTTPS is not affected by them.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Connect with an API token

```powershell
Connect-ZbxServer -Uri 'https://zabbix.example/api_jsonrpc.php' -ApiToken $token
Get-ZbxApiInfo
```

$token is the API token as a SecureString (create one under Users > API tokens; read it with Read-Host -AsSecureString). The connection is named after the endpoint's host and port and becomes the current server, so every later command uses it without -Connection.

### Example 2: Tell a refused credential from an unreachable server

```powershell
try { Connect-ZbxServer -Uri 'https://zabbix.example/api_jsonrpc.php' -ApiToken (ConvertTo-SecureString 'not-a-token' -AsPlainText -Force) -Name 'refused' }
catch { $_.CategoryInfo.Category; $_.ErrorDetails.Message }
```

The credential is proven before the connection is added: a token or password the server refuses ends the command with an AuthenticationError naming the server, and nothing is added. An unreachable server is a ConnectionError.

### Example 3: Connect with a user name and password

```powershell
Connect-ZbxServer -Uri 'https://zabbix.example/api_jsonrpc.php' -Credential $credential -Name 'admin' -NoDefault
Get-ZbxApiInfo -Connection 'admin'
Disconnect-ZbxServer -Name 'admin'
```

$credential is a PSCredential (Get-Credential). Connect-ZbxServer logs in (user.login) to prove it, and the session id is used from then on. -NoDefault adds the connection without making it the current server.

### Example 4: Work with a second server side by side

```powershell
$staging = Connect-ZbxServer -Uri 'https://zabbix.example/api_jsonrpc.php' -ApiToken $token -Name 'staging' -NoDefault -PassThru
Get-ZbxHost -Name 'web-01' -Connection $staging | Select-Object HostId, TechnicalName
Get-ZbxContext | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Servers
Disconnect-ZbxServer -Name 'staging'
```

A named connection that is not the default is reached with -Connection, by its name or by the object -PassThru wrote. The current server stays what it was.

### Example 5: Tell the connection where the server's trapper listens

```powershell
$lab = Connect-ZbxServer -Uri 'https://zabbix.example/api_jsonrpc.php' -ApiToken $token -Trapper 'zabbix.example:10051' -Name 'lab' -NoDefault -PassThru
$lab | Select-Object Name, Endpoint, Trapper, ApiVersion
Disconnect-ZbxServer -Name 'lab'
```

-Trapper is the server's trapper port as this machine reaches it, for the commands that speak the Zabbix protocol instead of the API (Send-ZbxData and the agent/proxy commands). Without it they ask the API for the active HA node's address, which may not be reachable from a client behind NAT.

### Example 6: Encrypt the trapper connection

```powershell
Connect-ZbxServer -Uri 'https://zabbix.example/api_jsonrpc.php' -ApiToken $token -Trapper 'zabbix.example:10051' -TrapperPskIdentity 'web-01' -TrapperPsk ./web-01.psk -Name 'tls' -NoDefault
Disconnect-ZbxServer -Name 'tls'
```

The TLS parameters are the trapper's, named after Zabbix's configuration (TLSPSKIdentity, TLSPSKFile, TLSCertFile, …): Send-ZbxData, Get-ZbxQueue, Test-ZbxItem and the other server-wire commands use them unless they are given their own. -TrapperPsk takes a SecureString or the path of a key file; the API's HTTPS is not affected.

## INPUTS

None.

## OUTPUTS

- `ZabbixConnection`: Represents one server the session is connected to: the SDK's ZabbixClient and the container that composed it through AddZabbix — logging to the host's streams, the shell's telemetry, and OTLP export when the module was imported with OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT set.
